title: Test cases of RWB-E2-023 have no story in the realignment plan
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx
description: Test Cases v7 holds 9 cases for legacy story RWB-E2-023, all Parked. RWB-E2-023 appears in neither the split plan legacy table nor the legacy index, and Template and Rules R6 does not list it among the already-cancelled keys. Its disposition in the 19-service target is therefore unstated.
evidence: 9 rows of Test Cases v7 with Story RWB-E2-023 and Status Parked; no entry in _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy and none in legacy_index.json.
proposed: Record RWB-E2-023 as cancelled with the other Epic 1 cancels, or give it a story; its 9 cases stay parked meanwhile.

title: Level vocabulary of Test Cases v7 is not the Template and Rules R7.2 vocabulary
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx
description: Test Cases v7 states levels System, Access, Resilience, Operational and Schema (and Rule table in the rule sheet). Template and Rules R7.2 section 16 asks for Unit, Component, Contract, Integration, End to end and NFR. The two vocabularies have no stated mapping.
evidence: Level column distinct values: System 1,234; Access 145; Resilience 58; Operational 19; Schema 1.
proposed: Keep the source Level column unchanged and add a Test level column in the R7.2 vocabulary, with the mapping recorded as an assumption.

title: Test Cases v7 covers 147 legacy keys of the 358 in the plan
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx
description: Test Cases v7 holds cases for 147 legacy stories (Epic 1, Epic 2, Epic 3, Epic 4, Epic 8 and ACE). The plan holds 358 legacy keys and 1,034 stories. The other 211 legacy keys have no case in the workbook; their cases exist only in section 16 of their story files.
evidence: 147 distinct Story values in the sheet; 358 keys in split_plan.json legacy; 1,416 test case identifiers in section 16 of the 147 integration stories alone.
proposed: Read the case inventory from section 16 of each story file for the keys the workbook does not cover, in a later test-data step.

title: A rule case names a route set, not the story or service that owns the rule set
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx
description: The 448 rule cases name their route set (Restructure, Settlement, Deed in lieu, Guarantee claim, Litigation, Asset disposal, Debt sale, Write-off, Deviations, Universal rules) and no owning service, story or rule package. The plan carries no story for a rule package, so a rule case cannot be tied to a story key.
evidence: Rule test cases sheet: 448 rows, Route set holds the ten names, no service column.
proposed: Name the executing service of every route set from Architecture v5 slide 3 and leave the story key empty for a rule case.

title: Neither workbook states the owner of a case
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx
description: Test Cases v7 and Regression Suite v6 carry Story, Epic, Module and route set, and no owner column. The realignment assigns one owning service to every artefact, and the Template and Rules R7.2 section 16 expects a case to belong to a story of one service.
evidence: No owner, service or team column in either workbook; 93 tables, 156 endpoints and 30 events carry an owner in the map.
proposed: Add a Service column holding the owning service of the case from the Microservice Ownership Map v1.

title: Two retired stories keep 20 live cases with no owning service
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx
description: RWB-E1-014 (decision log copy to the data lake) and RWB-TE-007 (Quartz scheduler) are retired under D-RCV-60 and get no new story, yet Test Cases v7 keeps 20 of their cases Live. Nothing states whether those cases are withdrawn or re-pointed at the replacement story.
evidence: 9 rows for RWB-E1-014 and 11 rows for RWB-TE-007 with Status Live; Template and Rules R6 retires both.
proposed: Mark the cases of the two retired stories as retired in the case sheet when the replacement stories are tested.

title: Integration test case count of the Integration Test Plan is not held in Test Cases v7
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Integration Test Plan v1.docx
description: Integration Test Plan v1 counts 1,416 test case identifiers in section 16 of the 147 integration stories, and Test Cases v7 holds no integration-level case at all. The two test documents therefore disagreed on the same cases.
evidence: Integration Test Plan v1 sentence on 1,416 identifiers; Test Cases v7 Level column holds no Integration or End to end value.
proposed: Add the -ITG case of every case the workbook already holds, as this version does, and let the plan count from the workbook.

title: Regression Suite Growth sheet stops at release E6
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Regression Suite v6.xlsx
description: The Growth sheet lists releases E1 to E6 and no wave 0 to 4 platform, integration or non-functional growth, while the target has 7 platform epics, 5 integration epics and 19 service stories in four waves. How the suite grows for the new platform and integration stories is therefore unstated.
evidence: Growth sheet rows: Release E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6; no platform or integration row.
proposed: Keep the Growth rows unchanged and state in the new Read me sheet that a new story's cases join the suite when its release ships.

title: No environment or pipeline stage is stated for the platform cases
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Strategy v3.docx
description: The 206 cases drafted from the 30 platform and integration stories that hold no legacy case need an environment and a stage. The test documents name DEV, SIT and UAT for the service cases and say nothing about where the platform baseline, Redis, DMZ gateway, schema and pipeline cases run.
evidence: 206 drafted rows; Test Strategy v3 names DEV, SIT and UAT only for the service cases.
proposed: State the environment and stage of the platform cases in the Test Data Plan, and keep the case rows environment-free until then.
